shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
We spend our whole lives learning how to be human, and then we die.
The things that terrify us most are usually just versions of something we've already survived.
You'll never know if you made the right choice because you'll never get to live the other life to compare it to.
Silence isn't the absence of sound—it's the absence of someone trying to fill it.
We call it "overthinking" when we're actually just thinking while anxious.
The people who seem to have it figured out are usually just better at pretending they're confused.
You can't miss something you never had, which is why some people are haunted by possibilities instead of memories.
Time feels slower when you're paying attention to it and faster when you're not—which means boredom is actually a sign you're being present.
We judge others by their actions and ourselves by our intentions, then wonder why everyone seems worse than us.
Your biggest problem right now probably won't matter in five years, but you won't remember it being this urgent either.
Most of what you worry about never happens, but some of it does—and there's no way to know which is which until it's over.
We're all just doing our best impression of knowing what we're doing.
The scariest moment in any relationship is when you realize the other person is actually just as lost as you are.
You don't become confident by feeling capable—you become capable by acting confident first.
Grief is just love with nowhere to go.
We treat our bodies like practice versions that we'll upgrade later, but this is the only one we get.
Adulting isn't harder than childhood—it's just that the problems got bigger and there's no one coming to fix them.
The people you envy are probably envying someone else, creating an endless chain of dissatisfaction.
Your phone has your entire life in it, yet you still feel empty sometimes—which means you're not actually looking for information.

darkjoke.thought: I told my friend he was adopted. He said, "I know, my parents told me." I said, "No, I mean by me—you're mine now."
My therapist asked if I have a support system. I said, "Yeah, my bed frame."
I love babies. They're so honest. They cry when they're sad, laugh when they're happy, and poop when they're nervous—basically they're just tiny drunk people.
My wife asked why I wasn't at our daughter's recital. I said, "I was, but I sat in the back so people wouldn't think she was mine."
I asked my dad why he never told me I was adopted. He said, "We're still working on a good time." I'm 34.
The doctor told me I have six months to live. I said I couldn't afford the payments. He said, "Make it three."
My girlfriend said she needs space. I told her to move to Alaska—seems like plenty.
I hate when people say, "Everything happens for a reason." Yeah, the reason is usually poor planning and bad decisions.
People ask me how I stay so calm. I tell them my emotions are on a subscription service I cancelled years ago.
My kid asked me what happens when we die. I said, "Taxes stop being your problem." He seemed oddly motivated to do his homework after that.
I told my friend his singing voice was unique. He was so happy until I clarified that unique means "one of a kind" like a crime scene.
My parents always said I could be anything I wanted. Turns out they meant unemployed.
I'm reading a book on the history of glue. I can't put it down.
My therapist said I'm in denial. I said, "I'm not." She said, "Exactly."
I tried to tell my family I'm going through an existential crisis. They said, "Join the club." Apparently I'm not special at that either.
My wife said I never listen. At least I think that's what she said—I wasn't really paying attention.
I asked the funeral director if people ever regret their final wishes. He said, "Not for long."
My boss asked why I'd been late three times this week. I said, "I have a very demanding life." He said, "You live alone." I said, "Exactly."
I told my son that lying has consequences. He said, "Like what?" I said, "You'll end up president." He's now a very honest teenager.
People say I'm too pessimistic. I disagree. I'm just an optimist with accurate data.
